---
title: Performance
description: Threads, GPU acceleration and memory use.
---

polars-umap is usually 2–12× faster than umap-learn, with no JIT warm-up; see the
[benchmarks](benchmarks.qmd). This page covers the settings that affect speed and memory.

## Threads

UMAP runs on a shared thread pool. Its size comes from, in order:

1. the `RAYON_NUM_THREADS` environment variable,
2. the `POLARS_MAX_THREADS` environment variable,
3. the number of logical CPUs.

When Polars evaluates several groups at once (`.over()` or `group_by()`), all of them share this
pool instead of each starting its own threads, so the machine isn't oversubscribed.

Pass `n_threads=` to run a call on a dedicated pool of that size, for example to leave cores free
for other work:

```python
pl.col("embedding").umap.fit_transform(n_threads=4)
```

With the default layout, the number of threads doesn't change the result.

## GPU

`gpu=True` runs the nearest neighbor search and the layout optimization on the GPU, through
[wgpu](https://wgpu.rs): Metal on macOS, Vulkan or DirectX 12 elsewhere. When no suitable GPU is
found, polars-umap quietly falls back to the CPU.

```python
pl.col("embedding").umap.fit_transform(gpu=True)
```

Setting up the GPU has a fixed cost, so it only pays off on larger data. In the benchmarks on an
Apple Silicon laptop:

- with the 0.5 layout, the GPU was 1.5–2× faster from about 10,000 rows;
- with the default 0.6 layout, it was only faster at a million rows (25 s against 32 s);
- on small data it was slower.

That's why `gpu=False` is the default. Measure on your own hardware and data.

## Memory

Peak memory is roughly the size of the input as `Float32`, plus the neighbor graph and the
optimizer state. That came to about 1 GB for 100,000 × 128 and 4 GB for 1,000,000 × 16 in the
benchmarks: the same as the upstream Rust implementation on its own.

To reduce it:

- **Store embeddings as `Float32`.** `Float64` input is converted, which costs an extra copy.
- **Select only what you need.** UMAP needs the full input column in memory, but not the other
  columns.
- **Reduce the dimensionality first.** For very wide vectors, a PCA to 50–100 dimensions before
  UMAP saves memory and time, usually with little effect on the result.

## Compared with umap-learn

polars-umap has no numba JIT compilation, which in umap-learn adds 10–12 seconds to the first call
in every new process. That makes polars-umap especially quick for scripts, notebooks that restart
often, and many small fits.
